content_list.content_text: On the night of January 5, 2020, accepting the Golden Globe for Best Foreign Language Film for Parasite (2019), South Korea's Bong Joon Ho spoke in his own language, with interpreter Sharon Choi at his side, and left behind a line that became a rallying cry: once you overcome the "one-inch-tall barrier of subtitles," you will be introduced to so many more amazing films. The message was aimed at American audiences, notoriously reluctant to read on screen, but it applied just as well to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. In more than nine decades of Oscars, no film in a language other than English had ever won the top prize. The 2010s are the story of how that wall was cracked, brick by brick, by filmmakers from Iran, Europe, Mexico and South Korea, until it came crashing down in a single February night.

information.contentText: In Parasite, how high up each family lives tells you which class it belongs to: the Kims live in a semi-basement with a window level with the sidewalk. It was this portrait of inequality in Seoul that broke through the "subtitle barrier."

content_list.content_text: Cinema from abroad always had a reserved seat at the party, but a seat set apart. Since the 1957 ceremony, when Fellini's La strada (1954) inaugurated the competitive race, there has been a Best Foreign Language Film category, in which each country submits a single title chosen by a national committee. Fellini, Bergman and Kurosawa won there, while the main categories remained, with very rare exceptions, reserved for English-language cinema. It was an honorable ghetto: it brought prestige, but rarely opened the way to Best Picture, Director or Screenplay. Anyone who wanted to compete with Hollywood on equal terms generally had to shoot in English. The shift of the 2010s began precisely when films shot in Persian, German, French, Polish, Hungarian, Spanish and Korean started breaking out of that pen.

quote.quote: The Oscars are not an international film festival. They're very local.
quote.author: Bong Joon Ho (interview with Vulture, 2019)

content_list.content_text: The first sign came from Iran. A Separation (2011), by Asghar Farhadi, follows a Tehran couple on the verge of divorce who become entangled in a legal case against the family of the woman hired to care for his father, a drama in which no one is entirely innocent. After winning the Golden Bear in Berlin in 2011, the film gave Iran its first Oscar on February 26, 2012. Five years later, Farhadi won again with The Salesman (2016), but he didn't go to collect the statuette. In protest against Donald Trump's executive order barring citizens of Iran and six other Muslim-majority countries from entering the United States, he boycotted the February 26, 2017, ceremony. Taking the stage in his place was Iranian American engineer Anousheh Ansari, who read the letter in which the director called the measure an "inhumane law."

information.contentText: Asghar Farhadi's drama about a divorce in Tehran won the Golden Bear and, in 2012, gave Iran its first Oscar, in addition to competing for Original Screenplay. Class, religion and guilt intertwine in a case that no one can judge with certainty.

content_list.content_text: Europe's auteurs responded with austere, far-from-easy films. Amour (2012), by Michael Haneke, about a couple of retired music teachers facing illness and death, won the 2012 Palme d'Or and arrived at the Oscars with five nominations, including Best Picture, Director and Actress for Emmanuelle Riva; it won Foreign Language Film for Austria. In 2015, Poland's Ida (2013), by Paweł Pawlikowski, shot in black and white in the near-square frame of old movie screens, gave the country its first Oscar in the category, with the story of a novice nun who discovers she is Jewish in 1960s Poland. The following year, Hungary's László Nemes made his feature debut with Saul fia (Son of Saul, 2015): the camera glued to the face of a prisoner forced to work in the crematoria of Auschwitz, with the horror always out of focus in the background. The film won the Grand Prix at Cannes and then the Oscar for Foreign Language Film.

information.contentText: Emmanuelle Riva and Jean-Louis Trintignant play the retired musician couple in Michael Haneke's film, winner of the Palme d'Or at Cannes and the Oscar for Foreign Language Film for Austria.
information.source: Publicity image: Les Films du Losange (via TMDB)

content_list.content_text: Meanwhile, Mexico was taking over the directing category from within. In 2014, Alfonso Cuarón won for Gravity (2013) and became the first Latin American to win Best Director. In 2015, Alejandro G. Iñárritu took Picture, Director and Screenplay for Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance) (2014); in 2016, he won Director again for The Revenant (2015), becoming only the third filmmaker to win twice in a row, after John Ford and Joseph L. Mankiewicz. In 2018, Guillermo del Toro won Picture and Director for The Shape of Water (2017). Together with cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki, the record holder with three consecutive Oscars, the "Three Amigos," as the press dubbed Cuarón, Iñárritu and del Toro, changed the face of the awards. There was, however, one catch: almost all of this was in English. Hollywood had learned to absorb foreign talent. What remained was to accept foreign films in their own language.

information.contentTitle: Ida wins the Oscar for Foreign Language Film
information.contentText: Paweł Pawlikowski accepts the statuette in 2015, Poland's first in the category. Four years later, he would return to the Oscars with another black-and-white film, Cold War.

content_list.content_text: That step came with Roma (2018). Cuarón returned to the Mexico City of his childhood, in the early 1970s, to tell the life of Cleo, an Indigenous domestic worker played by newcomer Yalitza Aparicio. The film, shot in black and white and spoken in Spanish and Mixtec, was financed and distributed by Netflix (the chapter on streaming tells that part of the story). After the company pulled its films from Cannes over a rule requiring a release in French theaters, Roma won the Golden Lion in Venice. At the Oscars, it received ten nominations, tying the record for a non-English-language film, and Yalitza became the first Indigenous Mexican woman nominated for Best Actress. On February 24, 2019, it took home three awards: Director, Cinematography (by Cuarón himself) and Foreign Language Film, Mexico's first. The top prize, however, went to Green Book (2018).

information.contentText: Yalitza Aparicio in Alfonso Cuarón's Roma. Shot in black and white and spoken in Spanish and Mixtec, the film gave Mexico its first Oscar for Foreign Language Film.

content_list.content_text: The 2019 race was perhaps the strongest in the category's history. Alongside Roma was Pawlikowski's Zimna wojna (Cold War, 2018), a black-and-white romance that crosses a divided Europe, inspired by the story of the director's parents; the film won him the directing prize at Cannes and three Oscar nominations, including Best Director. Also competing were Shoplifters (2018), by Hirokazu Kore-eda, winner of the 2018 Palme d'Or, about a clan of small-time Tokyo thieves that forces viewers to ask what, in the end, makes a family; Lebanon's Capernaum (2018); and Germany's Werk ohne Autor (Never Look Away, 2018), by Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck. The fact that two of the five Best Director nominees were competing with films in Spanish and Polish showed that voters no longer drew such a rigid line between "our" cinema and "theirs."

information.contentTitle: Alfonso Cuarón, director and cinematographer of Roma
information.contentText: In a conversation hosted by the Toronto International Film Festival, Cuarón explains how he ended up taking over the camera on his own film. The black-and-white cinematography, shot on large-format digital, earned him the Oscar in that category in 2019.

content_list.content_text: The Academy itself had been changing. After #OscarsSoWhite (the subject of the chapter on diversity), it announced in January 2016 a goal of doubling the number of women and members of color by 2020, and began inviting ever larger and more international classes: in 2019 alone, 842 invitations went out to professionals from 59 countries, half of them women. On April 23, 2019, came the symbolic change. The category was renamed Best International Feature Film because, according to committee co-chairs Larry Karaszewski and Diane Weyermann, the word "foreign" had become outdated within the global filmmaking community. The shortlist also grew, from nine to ten films. The first ceremony under the new name would be in February 2020.

content_list.title: From "Foreign Language" to "International"
content_list.description: Before the category existed, the Academy honored films from abroad with honorary statuettes: the first went to the Italian Sciuscià (Shoeshine, 1946), by Vittorio De Sica, in the late 1940s, and eight films were recognized this way through 1955. With competitive voting, starting in 1957, came the rule that has never changed: each country except the United States submits a single film, chosen by a local committee, and the dialogue must be predominantly in a language other than English. Until the mid-2000s, the film also had to be in an official language of the submitting country. Italy is the biggest winner, with 14 awards counting the honorary ones. The 2019 name change didn't resolve every contradiction: months later, in November, the Academy disqualified Nigeria's Lionheart (2018), by Genevieve Nnaji, for having too much dialogue in English, which happens to be Nigeria's official language. "International," after all, was still defined by distance from English.

content_list.content_text: No country, however, came as prepared as South Korea. In 2016, Park Chan-wook brought The Handmaiden (2016) to Cannes, transposing a Victorian novel by Sarah Waters to 1930s Korea under Japanese occupation. The country chose to submit a different title to the Oscars, but the film won the BAFTA for Best Film Not in the English Language in 2018. That same year, Lee Chang-dong adapted Haruki Murakami in Burning (2018), which won the international critics' prize at Cannes; in December 2018, it became the first Korean film to make the Academy's shortlist. Bong had already tested the West with English-language productions such as Snowpiercer (2013) and Okja (2017), but it was by going back to shooting in Korean that he went furthest. Until then, South Korea had never received a single Oscar nomination, in any category.

content_list.title: Parasite's Perfect Montage
content_list.description: Evan Puschak of Nerdwriter breaks down the sequence of about 60 shots in which the Kim family pulls off the scheme to get rid of the Parks' housekeeper, using a peach allergy to fake tuberculosis. The video shows how each shot adds a new piece of information, anticipates what comes next and calls back what came before.

content_list.content_text: On May 25, 2019, Parasite won the Palme d'Or, Korea's first. Ironically, the jury president was Iñárritu, who described the decision as "absolutely unanimous." In the United States, the film was released by independent distributor Neon, and the campaign became a phenomenon: Bong's interviews with interpreter Sharon Choi circulated on social media, the Kim family became a meme and, in January 2020, the cast won the ensemble award from the Screen Actors Guild (SAG), a first for a non-English-language film. Then came six Oscar nominations, the first in the country's history: Picture, Director, Original Screenplay, Film Editing, Production Design and International Feature. The Academy now had before it a film that American audiences were watching, discussing and understanding, even while reading subtitles.

content_list.title: Inside Parasite
content_list.description: The Park mansion doesn't exist. It was built from scratch as a set by production designer Lee Ha-jun, and Bong designed it as a world unto itself, full of corners where characters could spy on one another or hide from their employers. The houses of the rich and the poor were built on open-air lots, chosen with an eye to the position of the sun: the poorer the home, the less light it gets. Bong himself called Parasite a "stairway movie," and Lee admitted he had never built so many staircases for a film. The acknowledged reference is Kurosawa's High and Low (1963), in which the rich man lives at the top of the hill and the kidnapper watches him from below. Parasite has more layers: the Kim family climbs up to the Parks' living room, discovers that there are people living even further down, in the secret basement, and, on the night of the storm, descends step after step to their flooded semi-basement. The geography of the house is the social hierarchy itself.

content_list.content_text: On the night of February 9, 2020, Parasite won four Oscars. First, Original Screenplay, for Bong and Han Jin-won; then International Feature, the first awarded under the new name; then Director. In his speech, Bong recalled a line that had stayed with him since his student days and pointed to its author in the audience, Martin Scorsese, who received a standing ovation. Finally, Best Picture. For the first time in 92 ceremonies, the top prize went to a film not in English and, for the first time since Marty (1955), the same film took both the Palme d'Or and the Academy's highest honor. The "one-inch barrier" had not disappeared for audiences, but inside the Academy, it had fallen.

information.contentText: Jane Fonda announces the winner and Bong Joon Ho's team takes the stage at the 92nd ceremony. It was the first time a film in a language other than English won the Academy's top prize.

content_list.content_text: Brazil watched all of this from the audience. Anna Muylaert's The Second Mother (2015) earned Regina Casé and Camila Márdila an acting award at Sundance and was the country's Oscar submission for 2016, but it didn't make the final list. The team behind Aquarius (2016), by Kleber Mendonça Filho and starring Sonia Braga, protested at Cannes against the impeachment proceedings against President Dilma Rousseff; months later, the selection of Little Secret (2016) as the Oscar submission stirred controversy, with filmmakers questioning the impartiality of the committee that made it. In 2019, Kleber and Juliano Dornelles won the Jury Prize at Cannes with Bacurau (2019); Invisible Life (2019), by Karim Aïnouz, won the Un Certain Regard section and represented Brazil at the Oscars, again without a nomination. Nominations came through other routes: Boy & the World (2014), in animation, and The Edge of Democracy (2019), by Petra Costa, in documentary. In the foreign-language category, there had been no Brazilian nominee since Central Station (1998).

quote.quote: The most personal is the most creative.
quote.author: Bong Joon Ho, quoting Martin Scorsese (Oscar acceptance speech, 2020)

content_list.content_text: When the lights went down at the Dolby Theatre in February 2020, the decade ended with a clear tally. In ten years, Iranian, Austrian, Polish, Hungarian, Mexican, Japanese and Korean filmmakers had pushed the Oscars out of their comfort zone, helped by a more international Academy, by European festivals that served as showcases and by streaming money. None of this erased the inequality in distribution or much of the audience's resistance to subtitles. But Bong's message had gotten through to the voters: a film could come from anywhere and speak any language. The door was open, and the years that followed, told in the chapter The World Beyond Hollywood, would show who would walk through it.

information.contentText: Anna Muylaert's film about a housekeeper from the northeastern state of Pernambuco who lives in her employers' home in São Paulo explores, like Roma and Parasite, the class boundary within a single house. A prizewinner at Sundance and in Berlin, it was Brazil's Oscar submission for 2016.

movies.title: A Separação
movies.overview: Simin deseja mudar-se para garantir um futuro melhor para a família, mas seu marido Nader não quer por causa do pai doente. Ela entra com um pedido de separação e Nader contrata Razieh para cuidar de seu pai enquanto trabalha. Certo dia ao voltar para casa encontra o pai sozinho, desmaiado e amarrado à cama; Razieh aparece e os dois discutem, na sequência Nader empurra a mulher e dias depois, é notificado que Razieh estava grávida e teria perdido o bebê. Os dois terão que resolver a situação na justiça, e tem pontos de vista muito diferentes do que aconteceu durante a briga.

movies.title: O Apartamento
movies.overview: Emad e Rana são surpreendidos com o alerta para que eles e todos os moradores do prédio em que vivem deixem o local imediatamente, pois o prédio corre o risco de desabamento. Diante deste problema, eles passam a morar, provisoriamente, em um apartamento emprestado. É lá que Rana é surpreendida com a entrada de um estranho no banheiro, justamente quando está tomando banho. O susto faz com que ela se machuque seriamente e vá parar no hospital. Entretanto, é o trauma do ocorrido que afeta, cada vez mais, suas vidas.

movies.title: Amor
movies.overview: Georges e Anne são um casal de aposentados que costumavam dar aulas de música. Eles têm uma filha musicista que vive com marido e filhos em um país estrangeiro. Certo dia, Anne sofre um derrame e fica com um lado do corpo paralisado. O casal de idosos passa por graves obstáculos, que colocarão o seu amor em teste.

movies.title: Ida
movies.overview: Anna é uma órfã criada por freiras. Sua mestre lhe conta que, antes de completar seus votos, ela deve encontrar sua família, então ela vai visitar Wanda, sua única parente viva, antes que esta venha a falecer. Wanda diz a Anna que ela é judia, então as duas mulheres iniciam uma viagem, não só para encontrar a sua trágica história de família, mas para saber quem elas realmente são e aonde pertencem.

movies.title: Filho de Saul
movies.overview: 1944, campo de concentração de Auschwitz, durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial. Saul (Géza Röhrig) é um judeu obrigado a trabalhar para os nazistas, sendo um dos responsáveis em limpar as câmaras de gás após dezenas de outros judeus serem mortos. Em meio à tensão do momento e às dificuldades inerentes desta tarefa, ele reconhece entre os mortos o corpo de seu próprio filho.

movies.original_title: Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance)
movies.title: Birdman ou (A Inesperada Virtude da Ignorância)
movies.overview: Esperando ser levado a sério, Riggan Thomson, uma estrela envelhecida conhecida por interpretar um super-herói, tenta organizar uma peça da Broadway. Mas com as dificuldades da produção e a aproximação da noite de abertura, ele deve confrontar sua família, sua carreira e seu ego.

movies.title: A Forma da Água
movies.overview: Década de 60. Em meio aos grandes conflitos políticos e transformações sociais dos Estados Unidos da Guerra Fria, a muda Elisa, zeladora em um laboratório experimental secreto do governo, se encanta com uma criatura fantástica mantida presa e maltratada no local. Para executar um arriscado e apaixonado resgate, ela recorre ao melhor amigo Giles e à colega de turno Zelda, em uma aventura que pode custar muito mais do que o seu emprego.

movies.title: Roma
movies.overview: Na década de 1970, uma jovem trabalhadora doméstica indígena Cleodegaria "Cleo" Gutiérrez trabalha para uma família abastada de classe média do bairro de Roma, Cidade do México. À medida que as lutas domésticas e as restrições da hierarquia social se desdobram em meio a um pano de fundo de poderosos terremotos, revoltas estudantis e agitação política, a família luta para permanecer unida enquanto essas forças ameaçam separá-los.

movies.title: Guerra Fria
movies.overview: Durante a Guerra Fria na década de 1950, duas pessoas de diferentes origens e temperamentos, que são fatalmente incompatíveis, se apaixonam.

movies.title: Assunto de Família
movies.overview: Depois de uma de suas sessões de furtos, Osamu e seu filho se deparam com uma garotinha escondida. A princípio relutam em ajudar a menina, mas a esposa de Osamu concorda em  abrigar e cuidar dela depois de descobrir as dificuldades que ela enfrenta. Embora a família seja pobre e mal ganhem dinheiro com os pequenos crimes que cometem, eles parecem viver felizes juntos até que um incidente revela segredos escondidos, testando os laços que os unem.

movies.title: A Criada
movies.overview: Coreia do Sul, anos 1930. Durante a ocupação japonesa, a jovem Sookee é contratada para trabalhar para uma herdeira nipônica, Hideko, que leva uma vida isolada ao lado do tio autoritário. Só que Sookee guarda um segredo: ela e um vigarista planejam desposar a herdeira, roubar sua fortuna e trancafiá-la em um sanatório. Tudo corre bem com o plano, até que Sookee aos poucos começa a compreender as motivações de Hideko.

movies.title: Em Chamas
movies.overview: Durante um dia normal de trabalho como entregador, Jong-Soo reencontra Hae-Mi, uma antiga amiga que vivia no mesmo bairro que ele. A jovem está com uma viagem marcada para o exterior e pede para Jong-Soo cuidar de seu gato de estimação enquanto está longe. Hae-Mi volta para casa na companhia de Ben, um jovem misterioso que conheceu na África. No entanto, o forasteiro tem um hobby peculiar, que está prestes a ser revelado aos amigos.

movies.title: Parasita
movies.overview: Toda a família de Ki-taek está desempregada, vivendo num porão sujo e apertado. Uma obra do acaso faz com que o filho adolescente da família comece a dar aulas de inglês à garota de uma família rica. Fascinados com a vida luxuosa destas pessoas, pai, mãe, filho e filha bolam um plano para se infiltrarem também na família glamorosa, um a um. No entanto, os segredos e mentiras necessários à ascensão social custarão caro a todos.

movies.title: Que Horas Ela Volta?
movies.overview: A pernambucana Val (Regina Casé) se mudou para São Paulo a fim de dar melhores condições de vida para sua filha Jéssica. Com muito receio, ela deixou a menina no interior de Pernambuco para ser babá de Fabinho, morando integralmente na casa de seus patrões. Treze anos depois, quando o menino (Michel Joelsas) vai prestar vestibular, Jéssica (Camila Márdila) lhe telefona, pedindo ajuda para ir à São Paulo, no intuito de prestar a mesma prova. Os chefes de Val recebem a menina de braços abertos, só que quando ela deixa de seguir certo protocolo, circulando livremente, como não deveria, a situação se complica.

movies.title: Bacurau
movies.overview: Num futuro recente, Bacurau, um povoado do sertão de Pernambuco, some misteriosamente do mapa. Quando uma série de assassinatos inexplicáveis começam a acontecer, os moradores da cidade tentam reagir. Mas como se defender de um inimigo desconhecido e implacável?

content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 2010 to 2019
